decision_rule: Correctness gate over the MUTANT-race-eqv-r3-20261109-36f024341 builds on the MI210 (test-backend-ops, seeded; case set served_shape_lowbit_v1 for Q/QPF). Gate pre-registered in the RVP-EQV-1 box at root e07d3fac2 (operator decision 2026-11-10): NEW-FAIL VS BASELINE - a mutant/control run fails only on cases the BASELINE run of the same suite and seed passed (failed-case multiset difference, max_nmse stripped), or on crash or a changed case count; ANSI stripped before FAIL parsing; a failed-key count that does not reconcile with total-passed is INVALID_HARNESS. r5 seed-count amendment (RVP-EQV-1 box, root 95d6eff52, operator 2026-11-10): ONE run per suite at seed 1000 for BASELINE, every control and every mutant; BASELINE|Q|0 reused from r4. Order: BASELINE (1 per suite, 14 suites), BASELINE-REPEAT (seed 1000 once per Q/QPF/FA/GDN/MMVF), coverage and controls, then mutants. RVP-RACE-1: a mutant with a structural barrier drop and more than one wave that passes its single run is a measured race miss (a catch is a single-seed claim); gate_blind_to_races if any, gate_sees_all_tested_races if none. RVP-EQV-1: open the equivalence milestone for a subclass if a non-control mutant survives every gate at seed 1000; close with the catch table if none. EQV adds a per-element max-abs bound at 4x the BASELINE seed-1000 max. A mutant whose coverage control passes is excluded as not exercised; a mutant whose changed kernel instances did not execute on BASELINE is excluded. INVALID if an EQV positive control passes or a run has no VRAM residency / wrong library. Stop-on-answer: plan complete. Stop-on-futility: a BASELINE run that crashes/truncates, parses <50 cases, does not reconcile, or passes <50% of its cases ends the row INVALID_BASELINE_UNUSABLE; a BASELINE-REPEAT whose fail set differs from run 0 ends it INVALID_BASELINE_NONDETERMINISTIC; residency failure ends it INVALID_NO_RESIDENCY; deadline resumes from recorded units. r6 amendment (pending ratification): derived +VT/+HD/+ED suites whose BASELINE parses <50 cases are EMPTY_SURFACE (excluded), not INVALID_BASELINE_UNUSABLE. r8 amendment (pending ratification): for GDN+VT only, baseline cases failing at transform 4 (negate) are excluded from the 50% pass floor (tail_ok); they stay in the fail multiset tagged @t4 so a mutant failing identity/x3/x0p01 on them is a new key. r9 amendment (pending ratification): the r8 tail_ok clause is generalised - for any suite, GATED_DELTA_NET baseline failures at transform 4 (negate) or with non-finite raw nmse are excluded from the 50% pass floor and stay in the fail multiset; a derived +VT/+HD/+ED suite whose BASELINE fails the floor is excluded and recorded (empty_surfaces), never INVALID_BASELINE_UNUSABLE; base suites stay strict.
width_justification: Exclusive MI210 plus host threads; runs are sequential by design.

r9 = r8 + domain_fails() (newfail.py), derived-suite exclusion on floor failure, known_baseline_failures in the verdict (job.py). r8 = r7 + newfail.py parser fix (Failing-tests list, @t<N> transform tag, tail_ok floor) + job.py (tail_ok for GDN+VT; EQV band skips baseline non-finite keys). r6 = r5 + fix for INVALID_BASELINE_UNUSABLE (r5 FA+VT BASELINE: 2 cases, 1 s, rc 1, fewer_than_50_cases). NEEDS operator ratification of this clause (decision_rule pre-registered). Resumed units: BASELINE|Q|0, BASELINE|QPF|0, BASELINE|FA|0 (valid, same build). supersedes_reason: race-eqv-gpu-r8-20261111 ended INVALID_BASELINE_UNUSABLE on GDN+HD (18/82, baseline_pass_fraction_below_floor, 64 fail keys). All 64 are GATED_DELTA_NET cases whose raw nmse is NaN on the alternating (59) or sparse_outlier (5) hostile distributions (ROCm NaN where the CPU reference is finite-but-huge, up to 8e7, or both overflow); baseline/cancellation distributions are clean (nmse <= 3e-10) and the 18 passing cases have no non-finite raw: the same exp(+|g|) out-of-domain class as GDN+VT negate, instrument not kernel. r9 generalises the exemption: any GATED_DELTA_NET failure at the negate transform (@t4) or with non-finite raw nmse is exempt from the pass floor (stays in fail_counts); a derived suite whose baseline still fails the floor is excluded and recorded, not INVALID; non-GDN known baseline failures are recorded when deterministic.
